title: Ancient Trees in South Korea: 3 Cities to Explore
meta_description: A general's walking stick, a king's court rank, a traffic circle built around three ginkgos. 3 cities mapped, 11 trees, one a National Monument.
intro: South Korea's Cultural Heritage Administration keeps close enough tabs on its old trees to catch a legend in the act: an oak in Sillim-dong said to have grown from a general's walking stick in 1019 measured out, on survey, to about 250 years, a successor standing near where the legend took root. Seoul carries eight of the eleven trees mapped so far, among them the Siheung-dong ginkgos, two or three trees at the center of a traffic circle marking a vanished royal way station, and a Changdeokgung juniper the palace itself is built around. Busan holds a fortress pine and a stand of crape myrtles, eight hundred years old by tradition. An hour east in Yangpyeong, a ginkgo King Sejong is said to have granted a court rank turns the mountain road gold each autumn, and by most measurements is the tallest of its kind in the country.
